summary: Divergent scenarios then discriminating questions on champion adapter
hypothesis: Generating divergent scenarios first, then deriving discriminating questions from them, should improve information-gain and coverage by forcing the model to explore the solution space more broadly before committing to questions.
technique: A two-stage FM pipeline on the champion LoRA adapter: a first call generates divergent scenarios (solution-space exploration), then a second call derives discriminating questions from those scenarios — a structured "Lever C" info-gain decomposition.
result: Scored 0.305 on the full-30 eval (0 wins / 1 tie / 19 losses vs Sonnet), with specPass=100% but rubric scores of atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=3. This is below the champion adapter baseline and well short of parity; the divergent-scenario decomposition did not improve coverage or overall quality, so the run was discarded.
